question: A shopkeeper marked a toy car at ₹850 and sold it at a 15% discount, making a profit of 25%. Find the cost price of the toy car.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct relation between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) using ratio method:

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP ÷ 850 = (100 − 15) ÷ (100 + 25)

⇒ CP ÷ 850 = 85 ÷ 125 = 17 ÷ 25

⇒ CP = 850 × (17 ÷ 25) = 34 × 17 = 578

**∴ The correct answer is ₹578.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹850

Discount% = 15%

Profit% = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 CP = ?
 
 
 SP
 
 
 MP = 850
 
 

 − 15% (Discount)

 

 + 25% (Profit)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 850 × (100 − 15) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 850 × 85 ÷ 100 = 850 × 0.85 = ₹722.50

⇒ CP = 722.50 × 100 ÷ (100 + 25)

⇒ CP = 72250 ÷ 125 = ₹578

**∴ The correct answer is ₹578.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct CP and MP Relation

The fastest way to link Cost Price and Marked Price when both discount and profit are given is CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Markup Percentage

Markup is the extra value added to the Cost Price to fix the Marked Price. It is always calculated on the base of Cost Price: MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100).
